chain.label: Overly ambitious itinerary and media commitments
chain.trigger: the itinerary was overly ambitious... 51 hours of flying over 8 days, with no days off; media interviews scheduled for that evening in Ft. Wayne, Indiana, and the following evening in Massachusetts

chain.label: Thunderstorm with heavy precipitation advancing over the departure area
chain.trigger: thunderstorm began 0823... reflectivities in the vicinity of Cheyenne from around 40 dBZ to 50 dBZ; the accident sequence took place near the edge of a thunderstorm

chain.label: Strong gusty westerly crosswind on runway 30
chain.trigger: wind two five zero at twenty gusting twenty eight; there is evidence of significant crosswinds of 21 to 23 knots on runway 30 at the time of the accident flight's takeoff

chain.label: Density altitude of 6,670 feet at Cheyenne
chain.trigger: the density altitude at the time of the takeoff and accident was 6,670 feet msl... would have decreased the airplane's best rate-of-climb speed to 81 mph; with a climb rate of 387 feet per minute

chain.label: Airplane 96 pounds over maximum gross takeoff weight
chain.trigger: the airplane was 96 pounds over the maximum gross takeoff weight at takeoff... The additional weight would have increased the airplane's stall speed about 2 percent

caused_by.evidence: if he had been fully attentive to the preflight preparations, he might have questioned whether the numerous bags and other items being loaded on the airplane would result in an overweight condition

chain.label: Pilot's limited experience with high density altitude takeoffs
chain.trigger: The pilot in command had only performed a total of ten known takeoffs out of airports at elevations exceeding 4,500 feet msl, and only five of those flights were performed from airports over 6,000 feet msl

chain.label: Decision to take off into deteriorating weather
chain.trigger: the pilot in command's improper decision to take off into deteriorating weather conditions... when the airplane was overweight and when the density altitude was higher than he was accustomed to

caused_by.evidence: Contributing to the pilot in command's decision to take off was a desire to adhere to an overly ambitious itinerary, in part, because of media commitments

the only way to avoid being held up by the storm, and therefore to maintain the tightly scheduled itinerary, was to fly for several minutes in the deteriorating and potentially unsafe weather conditions associated with the storm
the pilot in command was aware of these adverse wind conditions prior to executing the takeoff... 'a twin Cessna just departed reported moderate low-level windshear plus or minus one five knots'
the pilot in command had limited experience operating out of high density altitude airports, such as Cheyenne, and that this should have prompted him to be cautious
when the airplane was overweight

chain.label: Rolling takeoff without a pretakeoff checklist; mixture not leaned, carburetor heat not checked
chain.trigger: The pilot's failure to stop at the end of the runway before his takeoff roll suggests that he did not perform a pretakeoff checklist, which would have included a magneto and carburetor heat check

caused_by.evidence: He said that the airplane did not come to a complete stop at the beginning of the runway, and that it was rolling when he gave the takeoff clearance

chain.label: Moderate turbulence, gusty winds and airspeed fluctuations during takeoff and climbout
chain.trigger: the airplane experienced strong crosswinds, moderate turbulence and gusty winds during its takeoff and attempted climb

caused_by.evidence: the winds were generally westerly at the surface and near-surface at speeds that varied between 15 and 30 knots
control problems associated with turbulence and gusty winds would have affected the airborne portion of the flight as well

chain.label: Right turn to the east after takeoff to avoid the storm, placing the airplane downwind
chain.trigger: the pilot in command decided to turn right immediately after takeoff to avoid the nearby thunderstorm and heavy precipitation that would have been encountered on a straight-out departure

caused_by.evidence: he turned about 1/2 mile after takeoff because of the approaching storm. The pilot in command of the accident flight also turned shortly after takeoff

chain.label: Pilot misjudged the margin above stall speed, misperceiving ground speed as airspeed
chain.trigger: the right turn into a tailwind may have caused the pilot in command to misjudge the margin of safety above the airplane's stall speed

caused_by.evidence: What was initially a crosswind during the takeoff roll and initial airborne phase became a tailwind after the airplane began its right turn... he may have misperceived the increased ground speed as an increase in airspeed
he may have had difficulty monitoring it because of airspeed fluctuations

chain.label: Failure to maintain airspeed; nose raised to compensate for the low climb rate
chain.trigger: the pilot in command failed to ensure that the airplane maintained sufficient airspeed during the initial climb and subsequent downwind turn to ensure an adequate margin above the airplane's stall speed

caused_by.evidence: the pilot may have increased the airplane's pitch angle to compensate for the perceived decreased climb rate, especially if the pilot misperceived the apparent ground speed for airspeed
the high density altitude and possibly the pilot in command's limited experience with this type of takeoff contributed to the loss of airspeed that led to the stall

This reduced rate of climb might well prompt a person who was inexperienced with high density altitude takeoffs to raise the nose of the airplane in an attempt to increase the rate of climb, thereby further decreasing the airspeed
Either or both of these conditions could have reduced the engine power sufficiently to cause a loss of climb capability
these wind conditions would make it more difficult to maintain a constant airspeed and rate of climb and could result in an unintended reduction in airspeed to below the airplane's stall speed

chain.label: Airplane stalled at several hundred feet agl
chain.trigger: resulting in a stall caused by failure to maintain airspeed

caused_by.evidence: the reduction in the climb speed to below the stall speed
the combination of the effects of the rain, the overweight condition, and the gradual bank angle of the airplane would have increased the airplane's stall speed from about 59 mph to about 64 mph

chain.label: Roll off on a wing and near-vertical descent
chain.trigger: it rapidly rolled off on a wing and descended steeply to the ground in a near vertical flightpath, consistent with a stall

caused_by.evidence: In-flight loss of control and subsequent collision with terrain

chain.label: Collision with terrain in a residential neighborhood
chain.trigger: The impact occurred approximately 4,000 feet north of the departure (upwind) end of runway 30 in a residential neighborhood

caused_by.evidence: collided with terrain after a loss of control following takeoff from runway 30

chain.label: Three occupants fatally injured
chain.trigger: The pilot in command, pilot trainee, and rear seat passenger (the pilot trainee's father) were fatally injured

caused_by.evidence: The impact was not survivable for the three occupants... traumatic injuries were the cause of death for all three victims
